product.amstrad-pc1640.summary: The PC1512 successor that added EGA graphics.
product.amstrad-pc1640.history: Amstrad expanded its PC-compatible range in 1987 with the PC1640, a development of the PC1512 for users who needed higher-resolution graphics. In September 1987, Personal Computer World listed a UK price of £799 plus VAT with an EGA monitor and one floppy drive. It was sold in the United States as the PC6400.
product.amstrad-pc1640.technical.video: The monitor determined which modes could be displayed. With the PC-ECD, the Paradise IGA and its 256 KB of video memory could display 640 × 350 EGA in 16 colours.
product.amstrad-pc1640.technical.memory: The boot and video firmware occupy separate areas. The manual places the system ROM at FC000h–FFFFFh, with mirrors at F0000h–FBFFFh, and the IGA ROM at C0000h–C7FFFh.
product.amstrad-pc1640.technical.verifie: BluMach includes the pc1640 profile. The hashes of the three ROM files match the library manifest.
product.amstrad-pc1640.technical.limitat: Boot and video modes with those ROMs remain to be validated in BluMach.
